page_title: Google Android Studio — Techbase STEM Academy
meta_description: Free Google Android Studio course: 72 lessons from Kotlin and Jetpack Compose to architecture, accessibility, Kotlin Multiplatform and Google Play. Techbase, Ibadan, Nigeria.
eyebrow: Free Course · Beginner → Advanced · Ibadan, Nigeria
hero_sub_html: Build real Android apps from your first install to the Play Store. 72 lessons covering Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, architecture, accessibility, Kotlin Multiplatform and publishing, ordered by difficulty.

about.label: About This Course
about.h2_html: From zero to published Android developer.
paras_html: Google Android Studio is the official tool for building Android apps, and this single course teaches you to use it from your very first install to publishing on Google Play. It follows every programme on Google's official Android courses page, arranged by difficulty: Android Basics with Compose, Jetpack Compose for Android developers, Modern Android App Architecture, Accessibility, Kotlin Multiplatform and the Google Play Store Listing Certificate.

Every lesson is written step by step with real code, expected output, practice challenges, a knowledge check and a mini project. Designed by Babatunde Awoyemi, Techbase Consultant Services, Ibadan. Free, always.
bullets_html: Android Studio setup, emulators, real devices, Logcat and the debugger
Kotlin from your first program to generics, lambdas and collections
Jetpack Compose: layouts, state, lists, theming, animation and testing
ViewModel, Navigation, Room, DataStore, Retrofit, Coil and WorkManager
Advanced Compose, performance, adaptive layouts, Wear OS and Glance
App architecture, dependency injection, offline-first design
Accessibility: TalkBack, semantics, contrast and touch targets
Kotlin Multiplatform for Android and iOS
Release builds, Google Play Console and store listing certification

kit.name: A computer
kit.info: Windows, macOS, Linux or ChromeOS that can run Android Studio. 8 GB of RAM is the minimum and 16 GB is comfortable.

kit.name: Android Studio
kit.info: Free from developer.android.com/studio. Lesson 02 walks you through the install.

kit.name: An Android phone (optional)
kit.info: The emulator is enough for almost everything. A real device makes testing more fun.

kit.name: A stable internet connection
kit.info: Android Studio downloads the SDK and Gradle libraries the first time you use them.

about.kit_note: Course content is original Techbase teaching material that follows the structure of Google's free Android courses. Each lesson links to the official codelabs and documentation, which are published by Google under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence (code samples under Apache 2.0).

phases.name: Phase 1 — Getting Started with Android Studio (01–05) · 5 lessons

lessons.title: Welcome to Android Development: What Android Is and How This Course Works
lessons.desc: Meet the Android platform, see how apps are built and shipped, and get the roadmap for every lesson in this course.

lessons.title: Download and Install Android Studio
lessons.desc: Check system requirements, install Android Studio on Windows, macOS or Linux, set up the SDK and take a guided tour of the IDE.

lessons.title: Create Your First Android App
lessons.desc: Use the New Project wizard, understand every file in the project and learn how Gradle builds your app.

lessons.title: Run Your App on the Android Emulator
lessons.desc: Create virtual devices, run your app, and master emulator controls, snapshots and troubleshooting.

lessons.title: Run on a Real Phone and Connect Your Devices
lessons.desc: Enable USB and wireless debugging, use adb, mirror your device and read your first Logcat messages.

lessons.title: Your First Program in Kotlin
lessons.desc: Write and run your first Kotlin programs in the Kotlin Playground and Android Studio: main, println, comments and string templates.

lessons.title: Create and Use Variables in Kotlin
lessons.desc: Store data with val and var, learn Kotlin's basic types, operators and type inference.

lessons.title: Create and Use Functions in Kotlin
lessons.desc: Write reusable functions with parameters, default and named arguments, return values and single-expression syntax.

lessons.title: Conditionals and Loops in Kotlin
lessons.desc: Make decisions with if and when, repeat work with for, while and repeat, and finish the Kotlin Basics practice problems.

lessons.title: Nullability in Kotlin
lessons.desc: Understand null safety: nullable types, safe calls, the Elvis operator, smart casts and when to avoid !!.

lessons.title: Classes and Objects in Kotlin
lessons.desc: Model real things with classes, properties, methods, inheritance, interfaces, abstract classes, data classes and enums.

lessons.title: Function Types and Lambda Expressions
lessons.desc: Treat functions as values: function types, lambdas, trailing lambda syntax, it, and passing behaviour as an argument.

lessons.title: Generics, Objects and Extensions
lessons.desc: Write type-safe reusable code with generics, singleton and companion objects, extension functions and scope functions.

lessons.title: Collections and Higher-Order Functions
lessons.desc: Work with List, Set and Map, and transform data with map, filter, fold, groupBy and sorting. Includes the Classes and Collections practice.

phases.name: Phase 3 — Your First Jetpack Compose Apps (15–22) · 8 lessons

lessons.title: Introduction to Jetpack Compose and Text Composables
lessons.desc: Build your first Compose UI: composable functions, Text, Preview, and the birthday card app.

lessons.title: Images, Layouts and Modifiers: The Business Card App
lessons.desc: Add images and arrange UI with Row, Column, Box and Modifier. Build the business card app from scratch.

lessons.title: Buttons and Click Behaviour: The Dice Roller App
lessons.desc: Respond to taps with Button, update the screen with remember and mutableStateOf, and build an interactive dice roller.

lessons.title: Debugging with Android Studio
lessons.desc: Find and fix bugs with Logcat, breakpoints, stepping, watches and conditional breakpoints.

lessons.title: State in Compose: The Tip Calculator and Art Space
lessons.desc: Understand state, recomposition and state hoisting by building a tip calculator, then apply it in the Art Space project.

lessons.title: Automated Tests for Your App
lessons.desc: Write local unit tests and Compose UI tests with JUnit to prove your tip calculator works.

lessons.title: Scrollable Lists and Grids: The Affirmations App
lessons.desc: Show data with LazyColumn and LazyVerticalGrid, model it with data classes, and customise your app icon. Includes the Grid practice app.

lessons.title: Material Theming and Simple Animation: Superheroes and 30 Days
lessons.desc: Make apps beautiful with Material Design 3 colours, typography and shapes, add simple animation, and finish with the 30 Days project.

lessons.title: The Activity Lifecycle
lessons.desc: Understand how Android creates, pauses and destroys your screens, and keep state safe across configuration changes with the Dessert Clicker app.

lessons.title: App Architecture and the ViewModel
lessons.desc: Learn why architecture matters, how the UI layer works, and move state out of composables into a ViewModel.

lessons.title: UI State, StateFlow and Unit-Testing the ViewModel
lessons.desc: Model screens with a UI state class, expose it with StateFlow, and write unit tests for ViewModel logic. Includes the Dessert Clicker ViewModel practice.

lessons.title: Navigation in Jetpack Compose: The Cupcake App
lessons.desc: Build a multi-screen app with NavHost and NavController, pass data between screens, share content, and test navigation.

lessons.title: Adaptive Layouts and Navigation Drawers
lessons.desc: Adapt your UI to phones, tablets and foldables with window size classes, adaptive navigation and a list-detail layout. Includes Reply, Sports and My City.

phases.name: Phase 5 — Data, Networking and Background Work (28–36) · 9 lessons

lessons.title: Coroutines and Concurrency
lessons.desc: Do many things at once without freezing the UI: suspend functions, launch, async, dispatchers and structured concurrency.

lessons.title: Get Data from the Internet: HTTP, REST and Retrofit
lessons.desc: Learn how HTTP and REST work, then fetch and parse JSON with Retrofit and kotlinx.serialization in the Mars Photos app.

lessons.title: The Data Layer: Repositories and Dependency Injection
lessons.desc: Separate data access from UI with repositories, then wire dependencies with a manual dependency injection container.

lessons.title: Load and Display Images from the Internet with Coil
lessons.desc: Show remote images with Coil's AsyncImage, handle loading and error states, and build the Amphibians and Bookshelf apps.

lessons.title: Introduction to Databases and SQL
lessons.desc: Learn relational database concepts and the SQL you need for Room: tables, keys, SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and JOIN.

lessons.title: Kotlin Flows in Practice
lessons.desc: Stream data over time with Flow, StateFlow and SharedFlow, collect it safely in Compose and test flows.

lessons.title: Persist Data with Room
lessons.desc: Store structured data on the device with Room entities, DAOs and databases, then read and update it in the Inventory and Bus Schedule apps.

lessons.title: Store Preferences with DataStore
lessons.desc: Save key-value settings with Preferences DataStore and finish with the Flight Search project.

lessons.title: Background Work with WorkManager
lessons.desc: Schedule reliable background tasks with WorkManager: workers, constraints, chaining, inspection and testing in the Water Me app.

phases.name: Phase 6 — Compose in Depth and Android Studio Tools (37–44) · 8 lessons

lessons.title: Thinking in Compose: Composable Functions and the Three Phases
lessons.desc: Shift from how to what: declarative UI, composable functions, composition, layout and drawing, and your first Compose essentials app.

lessons.title: Layouts and Modifiers in Depth
lessons.desc: Master Row, Column, Box, Scaffold, ConstraintLayout and the order of modifiers while you implement a real-world design.

lessons.title: Lazy Layouts: Lists, Grids and Scrolling Performance
lessons.desc: Build efficient scrolling UIs with LazyColumn, LazyRow and grids, using keys, content types, sticky headers and item animations.

lessons.title: Material Design 3: Theming, Dynamic Color and Typography
lessons.desc: Customise colours, shapes and type, support dark theme and dynamic colour, and style text with downloadable and variable fonts.

lessons.title: Animation in Compose
lessons.desc: Bring your UI to life: animate*AsState, AnimatedVisibility, AnimatedContent, transitions, Animatable and gesture-driven animation.

lessons.title: Android Views and XML Layouts
lessons.desc: Understand the classic View system: XML layouts, view binding, fragments and navigating between fragments.

lessons.title: Compose and Views Interoperability
lessons.desc: Use Compose and Views side by side: ComposeView in XML, AndroidView in Compose, and an incremental migration plan.

lessons.title: Android Studio Power Tools
lessons.desc: Get faster with Logcat, Layout Inspector, Database Inspector, Background Task Inspector, Profiler and Compose tooling.

lessons.title: Testing Jetpack Compose UIs
lessons.desc: Test composables with the semantics tree, finders, actions and assertions, and debug flaky tests with synchronisation.

lessons.title: Android Accessibility Fundamentals
lessons.desc: Learn who benefits from accessibility, how Android settings and services work, and the accessibility model behind TalkBack.

lessons.title: Accessibility in Compose: Labels, Touch Targets and Contrast
lessons.desc: Fix the three most common accessibility problems in Compose with semantics, minimum touch targets and contrast ratios.

lessons.title: Testing and Troubleshooting Accessibility
lessons.desc: Test with TalkBack, Accessibility Scanner, automated checks and lint, then review your app from your users' perspective.

phases.name: Phase 8 — Publish on Google Play (49–53) · 5 lessons

lessons.title: Prepare Your App for Release
lessons.desc: Get a release build ready: application ID, versioning, signing, Play App Signing, App Bundles, R8 and testing tracks.

lessons.title: Google Play Console and Store Listing Basics
lessons.desc: Module 1: create your developer account and app, publish a store listing and meet the baseline requirements for every listing.

lessons.title: Analyze and Explore Opportunities on Google Play
lessons.desc: Module 2: understand how users find your listing and test which elements drive the most installs.

lessons.title: Best Practices for Your Store Listing
lessons.desc: Module 3: build a consistent, benefit-focused brand story with strong icons, screenshots, graphics, text and localisation.

lessons.title: Custom Store Listings and the Certificate Exam
lessons.desc: Module 4: use custom store listings to attract and re-engage users, then prepare for the Google Play Store Listing Certificate exam.

lessons.title: Advanced State and Side Effects
lessons.desc: Hoist state well, build state holders, and use LaunchedEffect, DisposableEffect, rememberCoroutineScope, produceState and derivedStateOf.

lessons.title: Navigation Compose in Depth
lessons.desc: Go beyond basics: type-safe routes, arguments, deep links, nested graphs, bottom navigation, multi-module graphs and testing.

lessons.title: Custom Layouts and Graphics
lessons.desc: Build your own layouts with the Layout composable and draw custom graphics with Canvas, DrawScope and graphicsLayer.

lessons.title: Compose Performance
lessons.desc: Measure, debug and optimise: recomposition, stability, deferring state reads, baseline profiles and a scientific approach to performance.

lessons.title: Adaptive Apps for Phones, Tablets and Foldables
lessons.desc: Build adaptive apps with window size classes, canonical layouts, list-detail panes, navigation suites and foldable postures.

lessons.title: Wear OS and App Widgets with Compose and Glance
lessons.desc: Take Compose to the wrist with Compose for Wear OS and build app widgets with Jetpack Glance.

phases.name: Phase 10 — Modern Android App Architecture (60–65) · 6 lessons

lessons.title: Why App Architecture Matters: Principles and Layers
lessons.desc: Think like a building architect: separation of concerns, drive UI from data, single source of truth, unidirectional data flow and the recommended layers.

lessons.title: The UI Layer: State Holders, State Production and Events
lessons.desc: Define, produce and consume UI state, handle UI events correctly, and choose between ViewModels and plain state holders.

lessons.title: The Data Layer: Repositories, Data Sources and Source of Truth
lessons.desc: Design repositories and data sources, expose immutable data, handle errors and threading, and test the data layer.

lessons.title: The Domain Layer and Use Cases
lessons.desc: Decide when you need a domain layer, write use cases, and keep business logic reusable and testable.

lessons.title: Build an Offline-First App
lessons.desc: Design for no connectivity: reads, writes, sync strategies and conflict resolution with Room and WorkManager.

lessons.title: Dependency Injection with Hilt and Modularization
lessons.desc: Replace manual DI with Hilt, structure a multi-module project, and finish the architecture quiz.

lessons.title: Why Kotlin Multiplatform
lessons.desc: Learn what Kotlin Multiplatform is, ten reasons to adopt it, how it compiles to each target, and expect/actual.

lessons.title: KMP Project Structure: Targets and Source Sets
lessons.desc: Understand common code, targets, source sets, hierarchy and tests, and read a real KMP Gradle build.

lessons.title: Add Kotlin Multiplatform to Your Android Project
lessons.desc: Extract a shared module from an existing Android app and call platform-specific APIs with expect/actual and interfaces.

lessons.title: Integrate with iOS: Direct Integration and Swift Package Manager
lessons.desc: Consume your shared module from Xcode, add multiplatform dependencies, search klibs.io and publish through Swift Package Manager.

lessons.title: Migrate Room Database to Kotlin Multiplatform
lessons.desc: Move your database layer into shared code with Room KMP, a bundled SQLite driver and platform database builders, then take the KMP quiz.

lessons.title: Capstone Project: A Complete Android App
lessons.desc: Bring everything together: plan, architect, build, test, make accessible and prepare to publish a complete multi-screen app.

lessons.title: Android, Kotlin and Compose Quick Reference and Learning Roadmap
lessons.desc: A complete cheat sheet, interview preparation guide, certification map and study plan for your Android career.

steps.p_html: Start at lesson 01. You only need basic computer skills and basic maths. Kotlin is taught from zero.
Open Android Studio next to the lesson and type every example. Apps are learned by building them, not by reading.
Beginner (1–22), Intermediate (23–53) and Advanced (54–72). Use the level filter below to jump around.
Every lesson ends with a mini project you can push to GitHub, and the capstone lesson prepares a complete app for Google Play.
